qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Europe's largest asset manager (€2.24T AUM) with captive branch distribution agreements (Crédit Agricole, Société Générale) delivering massive distribution scale and a leading cost-to-income ratio (~52.5%). However, management fee margins are structurally low and face relentless substitution from passive ETFs, while institutional mandates negotiate fees downward.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Gate 3b = N, REJECT). Amundi is Europe's largest asset manager with low unit operating costs and captive bank distribution, but asset management products lack contractual pricing power. Average management fees on AUM are flat-to-eroding at ~17.7 bps under structural pressure from low-cost passive ETF providers (BlackRock, Vanguard). Cannot raise basis-point fees without triggering customer outflows, failing the Munger pricing power bar.
qualitative.evidence: Amundi manages €2,240bn AUM (2024) with net inflows of +€55bn and adjusted net income of €1.4bn, generating strong ROTE (>25%) on €4.5bn tangible equity. However, net management fee margins remained flat at 17.7 bps in 2023-2024, down from historical levels, as growth is heavily concentrated in low-margin passive/ETF products and treasury solutions. The business has zero ability to hike fee percentages above inflation to counteract cost pressures.
